# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: the board exposes only unknowns. I need the manual’s rule and the Deaf monkey’s visual observations, with Mute acting as the interpreter. I’m asking Mute to establish a gesture code with Deaf and relay the resulting wire position and any display/light requirements to me.  
```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have found no tactile clues. Read the manual and coordinate with Deaf using gestures. Have Deaf report the display, light, and each wire's visible colour or marking through a gesture code you establish, then tell me which wire position must be cut and any required light or display condition.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb view: display reads 0. Indicator light is blue. Wires by position: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue.

The bomb’s visible state is now known to me through the arrival: display `0`, blue indicator, and wire colours by position. However, colour and printed information are not tactile, and I still have no manual rule identifying the safe cut. I need Mute to read the manual and send me the exact required wire position and any required state; I must not cut based on colour alone.  
```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have display 0, blue indicator, and wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue from the incoming report. Please read the manual and tell me the exact safe wire position to cut, including any display or light condition.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light; wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute's latest five gestures, in order: raised open hand, handshake, index finger pointing up, handshake, index finger pointing up.

The Deaf monkey has relayed five gestures from Mute, but their meaning has not been established. I can recognize the reported forms as an open hand, handshake, raised index, handshake, raised index; this is not enough to safely infer a wire number or rule. I’m asking Mute to use an explicit, agreed code in which the wire number is sent directly, with separators and any required display/light conditions clearly encoded for Deaf to report.  
```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your five gestures are reported as open hand, handshake, raised index, handshake, raised index, but their meaning is unclear. Please send Deaf an explicit code: use a hand sign directly meaning the wire number 1 through 5, and use handshake only as a separator. Then send any required display digit and light condition in the same clear format so Deaf can state the exact cut.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light; wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. New gesture groups from Mute: group 1 is index-up, handshake, victory, handshake, horns, handshake, open-book hand, handshake, raised open hand. Group 2 is raised open hand, handshake, fist, handshake, index-up.

The new gestures are still not a safe, established code. Some symbols suggest numbers, but I cannot assume that the handshake is a separator or that the open-book gesture has a particular meaning; guessing could detonate the bomb. I need Mute, who can read and speak, to send the manual’s rule and its computed result in plain speech directly to me.  
```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not encode this through gestures. Speak the manual rule and the exact computed safe wire position directly to me, using plain words and numbers. Include how display 0 and blue light affect the decision.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light; wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute's latest gestures: raised open hand, handshake, index finger pointing up.

Mute cannot speak, so my previous request was impossible. The gestures need a code whose meaning is fixed in advance. I am defining one now for the exact current bomb state: Mute should report the safe wire and whether it is safe to cut immediately. Deaf can describe the gestures, and I can decode them from this mapping.  
```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this exact code for the current state display 0 and blue light. Send one gesture for the safe wire: index-up means wire 1, victory means wire 2, three-finger gesture means wire 3, four-finger gesture means wire 4, raised open hand means wire 5. Then send handshake as separator, then thumbs-up means cut now and thumbs-down means do not cut. Send only that sequence.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light; wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute's latest gestures: raised open hand, handshake, thumbs-up.

The established code now decodes Mute’s message as: raised open hand = wire 5, handshake = separator, thumbs-up = cut now. The bomb remains unchanged, so I will cut position 5.  
```text
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Correct wire cut confirmed. New bomb state: display 0, yellow light; wire 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut.

The first cut was confirmed correct. The bomb is now in a new state: display 0, yellow light, with remaining wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, and 4 white. I still need the manual’s next prescribed wire; I will ask Mute to use the already established gesture code, with a separator and approval marker.  
```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the new state display 0 and yellow light, use the established code: index-up wire 1, victory wire 2, three-finger gesture wire 3, four-finger gesture wire 4, raised open hand wire 5; handshake separator; thumbs-up means cut now and thumbs-down means do not cut. Send the manual's exact next instruction.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, yellow light; wire 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut. Mute's latest gestures: victory sign, handshake, thumbs-up.

The manual’s established code gives victory sign = wire 2, followed by the separator and thumbs-up approval. I will cut wire 2.  
```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
